newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to make global environment a priority.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to make global environment a priority.

text.p: Britain's main opposition party pledged on Saturday to seek tougher global targets for the emission of heat-trapping greenhouse gases as part of a drive to put environmental issues higher on the international agenda.

Foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook said Labour, favourite to win an election now less than four months away, would also aim to ensure that free trade for industry was compatible with safe trade for the environment.
A third priority for the party's environmental policy would be to secure a better share for Britain of the rapidly expanding market for "green" technologies, Cook said.
"Labour will bring a sense of urgency to the talks on how to save our globe," he said.
"No nation alone can opt out of global warming or hire its own private ozone layer. The common threat to each of us must be answered with common action by all of us," Cook added.
Talks on a new international climate agreement are due to conclude in Kyoto, Japan, in December.

Scientists warn that emissions of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, which warm the globe by trapping solar energy in the atmosphere, will lead to climate changes that could dangerously raise sea levels and hit world food supplies.
Cook was due to spell out Labour's plans in a speech later on Saturday to the Socialist Environmental and Resources Association. His office released excerpts in advance.

He said a Labour government would be in a pivotal position to provide leadership because within 12 months of the election Britain will take its six-month turn as European Union president and host summits of the Group of Seven industrial nations and the Commonwealth.
Cook announced the creation of a "Green Globe Task Force" to turn Labour's policies into a blueprint for action in office.
The advisory group will focus on three areas:

-- How best to turn Labour's commitment to cut emissions of carbon dioxide by a fifth by 2010 into a global agreement, and how to secure international targets to control nitrogen oxide emissions, which traffic congestion has increased.

-- Labour wants World Trade Organisation rules to recognise the primacy of environmental conventions. The advisory group will examine whether the right to refuse trade in products that damage the environment should also be extended to goods produced by processes that cause irreversible pollution.
-- How Britain can catch up with countries such as the United States and Germany that have taken a lead in developing green or environmentally-friendly products and technologies.
